sentences.text: Planohybodus is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the family Hybodontidae.
This animal is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
The type species, Planohybodus peterboroughensis, is estimated to have reached lengths of 2 to 3 meters.
A fossil tooth was found embedded inside an ammonite shell, proving it could attack hard-shelled prey.
The genus was formally described by Rees and Underwood in 2008.
Fossils of this shark have been discovered in both marine and freshwater environments.
Planohybodus belongs to the subfamily Hybodontinae within the family Hybodontidae.
Planohybodus peterboroughensis serves as the type species for the genus.
Another species, Planohybodus grossiconus, was found in England, Scotland, France, and Russia during the Middle Jurassic.
Planohybodus ensis is a species found in England and Spain during the Early Cretaceous.
The genus lived from the Middle Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous across Europe and the Indian subcontinent.
Planohybodus lived between 168.2 and 83.6 million years ago, from the Bathonian to the Santonian stages.
Records of Planohybodus from Mexico, Brazil, and North America are currently unconfirmed.
